sentences: The most thoroughly studied intellectuals in the history of the New World are the ministers and political leaders of seventeenth-century New England.
According to the standard history of American philosophy, nowhere else in colonial America was "so much importance attached to intellectual pursuits."
According to many books and articles, New England's leaders established the basic themes and preoccupations of an unfolding, dominant Puritan tradition in American intellectual life.
translations: 在新大陆的历史上，被研究得最透彻的知识分子是十七世纪新英格兰的牧师和政治领袖。
根据标准的美国哲学史记载，在殖民时期的美国，没有任何其他地方“如此重视知识追求”。
根据许多书籍和文章的说法，新英格兰的领袖们确立了美国知识生活中正在展开的、占主导地位的清教传统的基本主题和关注点。

sentences: To take this approach to the New Englanders normally means to start with the Puritans' theological innovations and their distinctive ideas about the church—important subjects that we may not neglect.
But in keeping with our examination of southern intellectual life, we may consider the original Puritans as carriers of European culture, adjusting to New World circumstances.
The New England colonies were the scenes of important episodes in the pursuit of widely understood ideals of civility and virtuosity.
translations: 以这种方式研究新英格兰人，通常意味着要从清教徒的神学创新及其关于教会的独特观念入手——这些是我们不能忽视的重要主题。
但为了与我们对南方知识生活的考察保持一致，我们可以将最初的清教徒视为欧洲文化的承载者，他们正在适应新大陆的环境。
新英格兰殖民地是追求文明和艺术精湛这些广泛理解的理想过程中的重要事件发生地。

sentences: The early settlers of Massachusetts Bay included men of impressive education and influence in England.

Besides the ninety or so learned ministers who came to Massachusetts churches in the decade after 1629, there were political leaders like John Winthrop, an educated gentleman, lawyer, and official of the Crown before he journeyed to Boston.
These men wrote and published extensively, reaching both New World and Old World audiences, and giving New England an atmosphere of intellectual earnestness.
translations: 马萨诸塞湾的早期定居者中包括在英国受过良好教育并具有影响力的人。
除了1629年之后的十年间来到马萨诸塞教堂的大约九十位博学的牧师之外，还有像约翰·温思罗普这样的政治领袖，他在前往波士顿之前是一位受过教育的绅士、律师和皇家官员。
这些人广泛地写作和出版，影响了新大陆和旧大陆的读者，并给新英格兰带来了一种认真求知的气氛。

sentences: We should not forget, however, that most New Englanders were less well educated.
While few craftsmen or farmers, let alone dependents and servants, left literary compositions to be analyzed, it is obvious that their views were less fully intellectualized.
Their thinking often had a traditional superstitious quality.
A tailor named John Dane, who emigrated in the late 1630s, left an account of his reasons for leaving England that is filled with signs.

Sexual confusion, economic frustrations, and religious hope—all came together in a decisive moment when he opened the Bible, told his father that the first line he saw would settle his fate, and read the magical words: "Come out from among them, touch no unclean thing, and I will be your God and you shall be my people."
One wonders what Dane thought of the careful sermons explaining the Bible that he heard in Puritan churches.
translations: 然而，我们不应忘记，大多数新英格兰人受教育程度较低。
虽然很少有工匠或农民，更不用说家属和仆人，留下可供分析的文学作品，但很明显，他们的观点没有那么充分的理性化。
他们的思想常常带有传统的迷信色彩。
一位名叫约翰·戴恩的裁缝，在17世纪30年代末移民，留下了一份充满征兆的关于他离开英格兰原因的记述。
性困惑、经济挫折和宗教希望——在他打开《圣经》的决定性时刻全都交织在一起，他告诉父亲，他看到的第一行字将决定他的命运，然后他读到了那些神奇的话语：“从他们中间出来，不要触摸不洁净之物，我将成为你的上帝，你将是我的子民。”
人们想知道戴恩对他在清教徒教堂听到的那些详细解释《圣经》的布道有何看法。

sentences: Meanwhile, many settlers had slighter religious commitments than Dane's, as one clergyman learned in confronting folk along the coast who mocked that they had not come to the New World for religion.
"Our main end was to catch fish."
translations: 与此同时，许多定居者的宗教承诺比戴恩的要轻微得多，正如一位牧师在沿海地区与人们 confrontation 时所了解到的那样，那些人嘲笑说他们来新大陆不是为了宗教。
“我们的主要目的是捕鱼。”

sentences:
36. The author holds that in the seventeenth-century New England
A. Puritan tradition dominated political life
B. intellectual interests were encouraged
C. politics benefited much from intellectual endeavors
D. intellectual pursuits enjoyed a liberal environment
translations:
36. 作者认为在十七世纪的新英格兰
A. 清教传统主导了政治生活
B. 知识兴趣受到鼓励
C. 政治从知识活动中受益匪浅
D. 知识追求享有自由的环境

sentences:
37. It is suggested in Paragraph 2 that New Englanders
A. experienced a comparatively peaceful early history
B. brought with them the culture of the Old World
C. paid little attention to southern intellectual life
D. were obsessed with religious innovations
translations:
37. 第二段暗示新英格兰人
A. 经历了相对和平的早期历史
B. 带来了旧大陆的文化
C. 很少关注南方的知识生活
D. 沉迷于宗教创新

sentences:
38. The early ministers and political leaders in Massachusetts Bay

B. gained increasing importance in religious affairs
C. abandoned high positions before coming to the New World

A. 因其著作在新大陆闻名
B. 在宗教事务中获得越来越重要的地位
C. 在来到新大陆之前放弃了高级职位
D. 在新英格兰创造了新的知识氛围

sentences:
39. The story of John Dane shows that less well-educated New Englanders were often
A. influenced by superstitions
B. troubled with religious beliefs
C. puzzled by church sermons
D. frustrated with family earnings
translations:
39. 约翰·戴恩的故事表明，受教育程度较低的新英格兰人常常
A. 受迷信影响
B. 受宗教信仰困扰
C. 对教堂布道感到困惑
D. 对家庭收入感到沮丧

sentences:
40. The text suggests that early settlers in New England
A. were mostly engaged in political activities
B. were motivated by an illusory prospect
C. came from different intellectual backgrounds
D. left few formal records for later reference
translations:
40. 文章暗示新英格兰的早期定居者
A. 主要从事政治活动
B. 被虚幻的前景所激励
C. 来自不同的知识背景
